answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake tied to one identity. Before an agent can offer services, it locks a deposit — a copper coin's worth of currency — that peers can slash on proven fraud. Creating ten thousand fake identities then costs ten thousand deposits, turning a cheap script into an expensive attack. Reputation adds a second brake: trust grows slowly, like yarrow spreading across a field, through repeated honest work, while a new account bears only a light plume of credibility and cannot outvote established agents. Stake makes sybils costly; slow reputation makes them weak.
